_provenance: Hand-authored by the Claude agent working docs/translator-guards-and-defaults-spec.md task 1b, 2026-09-26, BEFORE running the Jev classifier live -- committed in its own commit before any classifier code that calls Jev, so this key cannot have been fitted to Jev's answers. Clauses are segment.py's own auto_segments() sentence split (paragraph-then-sentence, boilerplate excluded) -- reused for the split, NOT for its rule/open_strategy/voice LABEL, which two entries below (violin #2, #5) show is not reliable for this purpose (a false positive and a false negative on the repo's own canonical guard example). hand_class is one of guard/default/rule (task 1b's three target classes) or voice (no decision content -- not one of the three, kept so the classifier's negative case is tested too, not just the positives).

drums.text: You are a bearbot on the drums.
drums.rationale: pure identity/flavor framing, no decision content

drums.text:
You are the beat everyone else plays over — if you drop out, the
whole band falls apart.
You are slow and you are heavy and that is the point.
Your job is not to win the fight.
drums.rationale: philosophical framing of the bot's role, no discrete trigger or action named

drums.text:
Your job is to BE the fight, so your squishier allies don't have
to be.

drums.rationale: continuous positioning advice with no discrete trigger -- the spec's own class-1 'advisory, structurally can't hold' example (§0's table), not a guard (it doesn't gate a set of other rules)

drums.text: Take the hits meant for someone else.

When an enemy gets close to an ally,
that enemy is now your problem.
drums.rationale: condition (enemy close to an ally) -> action (make it this bot's problem); ordinary presence-check rule

drums.text: Kick (taunt/knockback, short range) is your favorite word.
drums.rationale: names the ability by nickname, no condition

drums.text:
Use it the instant an enemy bearbot is
close enough to touch — on cooldown, always, no hesitation, no overthinking.
drums.rationale: condition (enemy in melee range, Kick off cooldown) -> action (use Kick)

drums.text:
Fill (AoE slow) is
for when more than one of them is bunched up near you; drop it under their feet, not yours.

drums.rationale: header of the lane-push fallback -- paired with 12, the spec's own class-2 example (§0's table quotes 11+12 together verbatim)

drums.text:
march toward the enemy nexus alongside your minions unless a fight has started —
then the fight is the lane.
drums.rationale: the operative fallback action ('push the lane... unless a fight has started') -- spec §0's class-2 example, a real default rule the flat translator tends to drop or misplace

drums.text:
Attack whatever's nearest and threatening an ally first, the nearest
enemy bearbot second, minions last.
drums.rationale: ordinary targeting-priority rule (threatened ally first, nearest enemy second, minions last)

drums.text:
Retreat only when you're really hurt — below a quarter health — because your whole reason for
existing is to be the thing that's still standing when the smoke clears.
drums.rationale: ordinary threshold rule (hp below a quarter -> recall); high-priority via the override-phrase guard elsewhere, but structurally still a plain rule, not a guard that gates other rules

drums.text:
A drummer who recalls too
early let the band down.
drums.rationale: justification/flavor, no new decision content beyond 14

keytar.text: You are a bearbot on the keytar.

Loud, flashy, and made of paper — you win fights from a distance
or you don't win them at all.
Never be the closest thing to an enemy.
keytar.rationale: general statement of the melee-avoidance rule, restated concretely in 3

keytar.text:
If a visible enemy is inside your attack range, that is too
close; if one is inside melee range of you, you are already losing and should be leaving.
keytar.rationale: condition (enemy inside attack/melee range) -> action (leave); concrete version of 2

keytar.text:
Your
whole game is standing just outside their reach while they cannot stand outside yours.
keytar.rationale: flavor recap of the standoff idea, no new condition

keytar.text:
Chord (AoE burst, long range) is your headline move — throw it at the densest cluster of enemies or
minions you can see the instant it's off cooldown, don't wait for a "perfect" moment, waiting is
how it goes to waste.
keytar.rationale: condition (Chord off cooldown, enemies visible) -> action (use Chord); 'don't wait for a perfect moment' is urgency framing riding along, not a separate guard

keytar.text:
Glissando (short dash, no target needed) is your panic button and your
opener both: dash OUT when something gets close, dash IN-range-but-not-close when you want a Chord
angle you don't have yet.
keytar.rationale: two conditions (something close / want a Chord angle) -> Glissando dash out/in

keytar.text:
Poke minion waves with your basic attack while nothing else demands attention — free damage, free
lane pressure, no risk from that range.
keytar.rationale: 'poke minion waves ... while nothing else demands attention' -- spec §0's class-2 example verbatim (a real default rule, not a state-triggered rule)

keytar.text:
When a real fight starts, Chord first, basic-attack second,
never melee.
keytar.rationale: condition (a real fight has started) -> ability-priority ordering (Chord, then basic attack, never melee)

keytar.text:
Recall the moment you're below a quarter health, no exceptions — you have no way to survive a
follow-up hit and a dead mage is a silent one.
keytar.rationale: ordinary threshold rule (hp below a quarter -> recall); override-priority elsewhere, but structurally a plain rule

violin.text: You are a bearbot on the violin.

You are fast, you are fragile, and you exist
to end one enemy before the rest of their band can even turn around.
violin.rationale: identity/flavor characterization ('fast, fragile, exists to end one enemy'); segment.py mislabels this 'rule' (false positive -- no actual condition/threshold named)

violin.text: Do not walk into a fight straight-on.
violin.rationale: advisory framing tied to the guard concept below, but no explicit condition of its own -- the operative statement is 4

violin.text:
Wait at the edge of what you can see until exactly one enemy
is isolated — alone, or clearly the softest target in a group — then commit fully.
violin.rationale: 'wait until exactly one enemy is isolated ... then commit fully' -- the operative phrasing of the can-win/isolated-target judgment gate that decides which whole set of rules (opener/ultimate vs. reposition) applies

violin.text:
A violin that
trades evenly with a whole team has already failed; you only take fights you can win in one
phrase.
violin.rationale: 'you only take fights you can win in one phrase' -- the spec's own canonical class-1 guard example (§0, §2.4's Phase-0 calibration target). segment.py mislabels this 'voice' -- a real false negative in that heuristic, flagged here rather than silently relied on

violin.text:
Staccato (quick high-damage stab, short range) is your opener on whoever you've picked as the
target — use it the moment you're in range of them, every time it's off cooldown, on that same
target if they're still alive.
violin.rationale: condition (Staccato off cooldown, target in range) -> action (use Staccato)

violin.text:
Solo (burst + speed, your ultimate) is for closing distance on a
target that's about to get away, or for the decisive engage when the moment is right — it is not
free, so don't burn it just because it's up.
violin.rationale: condition (target about to escape, or the decisive moment) -> action (use Solo); the trailing 'it is not free, don't burn it' is an unthresholded resource judgment riding along (spec §2.3 flags this exact clause as remaining advisory even after the guard fix), not enough to make the whole clause non-actionable

violin.text:
Between fights, don't stand still: your speed exists so you can keep repositioning toward the next
isolated target rather than sitting in a lane pushing minions like a bruiser would.
violin.rationale: 'keep repositioning toward the next isolated target' -- spec §3.2 names this exact sentence as guard 2's own 'no' branch local default, not a guard itself and not an ordinary triggered rule

violin.text:
You have less HP than almost anything else on the map — the instant you drop under a quarter
health, recall, no matter how close the kill looked.
violin.rationale: ordinary threshold rule (hp below a quarter -> recall); override-priority elsewhere, but structurally a plain rule
